column1: # TITLE: High resolution analysis of non-small cell lung cancer cell lines by whole genome tiling path array CGH

# SUMMARY: Chromosomal regions harboring tumor suppressors and oncogenes are often deleted or amplified. Array comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) detects segmental DNA copy number alterations in tumor DNA relative to a normal control. The recent development of a bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) array
column2: that spans the human genome in a tiling path manner with >32
column4: has facilitated whole genome profiling at an unprecedented resolution. Using this technology
column5: we comprehensively describe and compare the genomes of 28 commonly used non-small cell lung carcinoma cell models
column8: and 1 large cell carcinoma. Analysis at such resolution not only provided a detailed genomic alteration template for each of these model cell lines
column9: but revealed novel regions of frequent duplication and deletion. Significantly
column10: a detailed analysis of chromosome 7 identified 6 distinct regions of alterations across this chromosome implicating the presence of multiple novel oncogene loci on this chromosome. As well
column11: a comparison between the squamous and adenocarcinoma cells revealed alterations common to both subtypes
column12: such as the loss of 3p and gain of 5p
column13: in addition to multiple hotspots more frequently associated with only one subtype. Interestingly
column15: which is known to be amplified in both subtypes
column16: showed two distinct regions of alteration
column17: one frequently altered in squamous and one more frequent altered in adenocarcinoma. In summary
column18: our data demonstrates the unique information generated by high resolution analysis of NSCLC genomes and uncovers the presence of genetic alterations prevalent in the different NSCLC subtypes. Keywords: array CGH
